correctness.rationale: The dissipative spectral-projection lemma follows from contractivity and positive loss; the one-body star splitting gives complete eigenvalue sectors. The W tensor W detector Gram has strictly positive eigenvalues (L-1)/L and (L-2)/L for L>=3, and its inverse gives (2L-1)/(L^2(L-1)). At equal hopping all sector collisions are resolved including the zero-energy radial vector; at unequal hopping extra 2:1 collisions are rank-preserving because radial and zero-sum leaf detector images are orthogonal. Independent diagonalization, sitewise projector and lossy evolution checks passed (25 models, 950 basis-site probabilities and 12 survival checks). Assumptions exclude L=2 and zero losses; numerics are corroboration not proof.

value.rationale: Pair collision/reaction on finite star networks is a natural two-excitation transport question. The precise equal-speed resonance causes a nontrivial 2L-1-dimensional change in protected space and a sharp transition from 1/2 to certain eventual reaction for hub-leaf preparations under arbitrarily small speed mismatch. The complete localized reaction law also separates hub/leaf from leaf/leaf geometries, independently of all positive site-dependent loss rates. Unlike a parameter-renaming or single numerical value, this resolves an infinite family with a physically meaningful symmetry-breaking boundary. Limitations include ideal coherent dynamics and no finite-time uniformity.
